name: six-face-aimed-run
description: The DEFAULT six-face run in policy mode, with the T-018 relative-geometry clauses. Same shape as six-face-full-run.json (hold fire, hold right while the world scrolls, hop, dodge a houndframe's plant) plus the three things the old grammar could not say: TILT THE GUN UP when the nearest hostile above the firing line is meaningfully above it (the game's aim is 8-way, so a level shot cannot reach the 4.6/7.2 lanes at all — see docs/playtests/2026-08-gate-fight-harness.md); FACE the side that hostile is on during a gate, since facing and moving are the same key; and JUMP AT THE LIP of a hole instead of hopping into it. Note rules 4/5 lean on the documented `99` sentinel on purpose: with nothing above and nothing near, threat.dx>2 reads true, so the bot drifts toward the pivot during the post-clear ritual rather than standing still. MEASURED, NOT ASPIRATIONAL (2026-08-01, task/T-009's tree pinned at 8751, --deterministic, 1440x900, 245 s cap): this policy clears wave gate 1 without spending a life and clears wave gate 2 — both of which the aimless script never did on any tree — and then dies on face 3. It does NOT reach VICTORY. Per-tick aim quality against the same fights: the gun points at a hostile on 20-29% of gate-1 ticks and 28% of gate-2 ticks, against 8.8% / 12.0% for the aimless policy. Run-to-run spread is real (the two variants either side of the shipped hop guard reached face 3 and gate 2 respectively), so read the structural outcomes, not one run's numbers.
